entries.text: You have the right to work, but never to the fruit of work.
Set thy heart upon thy work, but never on its reward.
There is neither this world, nor the world beyond, nor happiness for the one who doubts.
The soul is neither born, and nor does it die.
A gift is pure when it is given from the heart to the right person at the right time, and when we expect nothing in return.
Whatever happened, happened for the good. Whatever is happening, is happening for the good. Whatever will happen, will also happen for the good.
The mind is restless, Arjuna; it is turbulent, strong, and stubborn. Yet it can be trained, through practice and dispassion.
When meditation is mastered, the mind is unwavering like the flame of a lamp in a windless place.
Perform your obligatory duty, because action is indeed better than inaction.
It is better to strive in one's own dharma than to succeed in the dharma of another.
One who has control over the mind is tranquil in heat and cold, in pleasure and pain, and in honor and dishonor.
Pleasure from the senses seems like nectar at first, but it is bitter as poison in the end.
Reshape yourself through the power of your will.
Those who have conquered themselves live in peace, alike in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, praise and blame.
A person is said to have achieved yoga when his desire for sense gratification does not enter the mind.
No one who does good work will ever come to a bad end, either here or in the world to come.
Whatever happened was good, what's happening is going well, whatever will happen, shall also be good.
The wise unify their consciousness and abandon attachment to the fruits of action.
Let not the fruits of action be your motive.
For one who has conquered the mind, the mind is the best of friends; but for one who has failed to do so, the mind remains the greatest enemy.
Man is made by his belief. As he believes, so he is.
Whatever you do, make it an offering to me — the food you eat, the sacrifices you make, the help you give.
Delusion arises from anger. The mind is bewildered by delusion. Reasoning is destroyed when the mind is bewildered.
Seek refuge in the attitude of detachment and you will amass the wealth of spiritual awareness.
Perform every action sacredly. Be free from all attachments to the results.
Your own self-realization is the greatest service you can render the world.
Calmness, gentleness, silence, self-restraint, and purity: these are the disciplines of the mind.
There is more happiness in doing one's own path without excellence than in doing another's path well.
As the heat of a fire reduces wood to ashes, the fire of knowledge burns to ashes all karma.
The senses are higher than the body; the mind is higher than the senses; above the mind is the intellect; and above the intellect is the Self.
